fullPassage: In the workplace, it’s vital that communication go both ways. People must be able to ask questions and offer critiques and ideas. Ideally, they should be able to do so with all managers, up to the CEO. At new employee college, we’d say to the participants, “You will take out of this day what you put into it. If you don’t ask questions, you won’t get answers.” I look back now and realize that this was crucial early stage-setting for the success of the company. It gave people at all levels license to freely ask for clarification, whether about something they were expected to do or about a decision made by management. Not only did this mean they were better informed, but over time it instilled throughout the company a culture of curiosity. That meant managers often gained important insights because someone had asked a really good question.

❌ ③ loudly(큰 소리로): 소리 크기와 관련된 말로 의미축이 다름
✅ ④ reluctantly(마지못해): 거리낌 없이(freely)의 반의어로 가장 적절 ←정답
det.tip: freely(자유롭게, 거리낌 없이) ↔ reluctantly(마지못해, 꺼리며)

questions.passage: In the workplace, it’s vital that communication go both ways. People must be able to ask questions and offer critiques and ideas. Ideally, they should be able to do so with all managers, up to the CEO. At new employee college, we’d say to the participants, “You will take out of this day what you put into it. If you don’t ask questions, you won’t get answers.” I look back now and realize that this was crucial early stage-setting for the success of the company. It gave people at all levels license to freely ask for clarification, whether about something they were expected to do or about a decision made by management. Not only did this mean they were better informed, but over time it instilled throughout the company a culture of curiosity. That meant managers often gained <u>important</u> insights because someone had asked a really good question.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 <u>important</u>와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: important(중요한) ↔ trivial(사소한).
det.analysis:
✅ ① trivial(사소한): 중요한(important)의 반의어로 가장 적절 ←정답
❌ ② essential(필수적인): important의 유의어라 반의어가 아님
❌ ③ distant(멀리 떨어진): 거리와 관련된 말로 의미축이 다름
❌ ④ heavy(무거운): 무게와 관련된 말로 의미축이 다름
det.tip: important(중요한) ↔ trivial(사소한, 하찮은)

questions.passage:
(A) During the meeting, employees are encouraged to <u>ask</u> questions whenever they do not understand something. A good question often reveals what the whole team has missed.

(B) If you need extra time to finish the report, you should <u>ask</u> your manager for it directly. It is always better to <u>ask</u> for help than to stay silent.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B)의 밑줄 친 ask의 의미로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A)의 ask는 '질문하다(pose a question)', (B)의 ask는 '요청하다·부탁하다(request)'.
det.analysis:
❌ ① (A) 요청하다 — (B) 질문하다: (A)와 (B)의 뜻이 서로 뒤바뀜
✅ ② (A) 질문하다 — (B) 요청하다: (A)는 'ask questions(질문을 하다)', (B)는 'ask ~ for it / ask for help(무언가를 요청·부탁하다)'을 뜻함 ←정답
❌ ③ (B)가 '대답하다'가 아니라 '요청하다'
❌ ④ (A)가 '방문하다'가 아니라 '질문하다'
det.tip: ask: 'ask questions(질문하다)'와 'ask for ~(요청하다)'는 뜻이 다른 다의어 — 문맥으로 구분

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "to gradually establish an idea or feeling in a person's mind"

det.korean: instill = (생각·감정을) 서서히 심어 주다, 스며들게 하다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① conceal(숨기다): '감추다'라는 뜻으로 정의와 불일치
❌ ② abandon(버리다): '포기하다'라는 뜻으로 정의와 불일치
❌ ③ exaggerate(과장하다): '부풀리다'라는 뜻으로 정의와 불일치
✅ ④ instill(서서히 심어 주다): '어떤 생각이나 감정을 사람의 마음에 서서히 자리 잡게 하다'라는 정의에 정확히 부합 ←정답
det.tip: instill an idea = 생각을 서서히 심어 주다 (본문: instilled a culture of curiosity)

questions.passage: Not only did this mean they were better __________ (inform), but over time it instilled throughout the company a culture of curiosity.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로, 1단어)

inform → ____

det.korean: be동사(were) 뒤에서 '~한 상태가 되다'라는 수동·완료의 의미를 나타내므로 과거분사 informed로 바꾼다.
det.analysis: 빈칸 앞에 be동사 were가 있어요. 'be동사 + 과거분사(p.p.)'는 '~된 상태이다'라는 뜻이에요. 여기서는 사람들이 '더 잘 알게 된' 상태를 나타내야 하므로 inform을 과거분사 informed로 바꿔 'they were better informed(그들은 더 잘 알게 되었다)'가 됩니다.
det.tip: be동사(were) + 과거분사(informed) = ~된 상태이다. inform → informed

questions.passage: I look back now and realize that this was crucial early stage-setting for the __________ (succeed) of the company. It gave people at all levels license to freely ask for clarification.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로, 1단어)

succeed → ____

det.korean: 관사 the의 수식을 받고 전치사 of 앞에 오는 명사 자리이므로 명사형 success로 바꾼다.
det.analysis: 빈칸 앞에 관사 the가 있고 뒤에 'of the company'가 이어져요. 'the ___ of ~'는 '~의 …'라는 명사 자리이므로 동사 succeed를 명사형 success로 바꿔야 해요. 'the success of the company(회사의 성공)'가 됩니다.
det.tip: 동사 succeed → 명사 success. the + 명사 + of 구조

Ideally, they should be able to do so with all managers, up to the CEO. At new employee college, we’d say to the participants, “You will take out of this day what you put into it. If you don’t ask questions, you won’t get answers.” I look back now and realize that this was crucial early stage-setting for the success of the company. Not only did this mean they were better informed, but over time it instilled throughout the company a culture of curiosity. That meant managers often gained important insights because someone had asked a really good question.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 양방향으로(both ways). 소통은 위아래 '양방향으로' 이루어져야 한다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① only upward(위쪽으로만): 다음 문장에서 CEO에게까지 질문할 수 있어야 한다며 위아래 모두를 말하므로 '위로만'은 부적절
❌ ② through email(이메일로): 소통 수단은 글의 관심사가 아님
✅ ③ both ways(양방향으로): 사람들이 질문·비판·아이디어를 낼 수 있어야 한다는 뒤 문장과 이어져 소통이 '양방향'이어야 함을 나타냄 ←정답
❌ ④ once a year(1년에 한 번): 빈도는 글의 논지와 무관
det.tip: communication go both ways = 소통이 양방향으로 이루어지다

questions.passage: In the workplace, it’s vital that communication go both ways. People must be able to ask questions and offer critiques and ideas. Ideally, they should be able to do so with all managers, up to the CEO. At new employee college, we’d say to the participants, “You will take out of this day what you put into it. If you don’t ask questions, you won’t get answers.” I look back now and realize that this was crucial early stage-setting for the success of the company. It gave people at all levels license to freely ask for clarification, whether about something they were expected to do or about a decision made by management. Not only did this mean they were better informed, but over time it instilled throughout the company a culture of curiosity. That meant managers often gained important insights because someone had asked __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 정말 좋은 질문(a really good question). 누군가 '정말 좋은 질문'을 던진 덕분에 관리자들이 통찰을 얻었다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① for a pay raise(임금 인상을 위해): 글은 임금이 아니라 질문의 가치를 말함
✅ ② a really good question(정말 좋은 질문): 글 전체가 좋은 질문의 힘을 강조하므로, 관리자들이 통찰을 얻은 이유는 누군가 '정말 좋은 질문'을 했기 때문 ←정답
❌ ③ the same thing twice(같은 것을 두 번): 반복은 글의 논지와 무관
❌ ④ to leave early(일찍 떠나기 위해): 문맥과 무관
det.tip: 글의 결론: someone had asked a really good question(누군가 정말 좋은 질문을 했다)
